"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-047-DEVELOPMENT-RULINGS-001__B00894_2f3a134d4a26","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Guest relationship","source_id":"M050-SRC-047-DEVELOPMENT-RULINGS-001","source_text":"<!--@27.2¶2-->
The Red Fox’s Carcass Claim is the principal example.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-ECOLOGY-001__B00249_4159b691c2e9","block_type":"table_row","section":"9.1 Environmental opportunities and pressures","source_id":"M050-SRC-ECOLOGY-001","source_text":"| Overhead Layer       | Seed heads, nests, signs, cables, branches, wind-caught objects.     | Wind, raptors, maintenance, fall and isolation risk.            | Primarily Squirrel; occasional guest-species access.                |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00706_452af83628c4","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.2 Reader-facing species convention","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Owl; Sparrow; Toad; Firefly Family; Groundhog; Turtle; Bumblebee Household; Mole; Bat; Pigeon; Skunk; Opossum | Raccoon; Crow; Fox; Weasel; Hedgehog; Snake; Mink |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00714_97db7bfe9055","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Owl                 | Watchkeeper   | Night Sky-watch                   | Earlier and clearer Telegraph in eligible night Home MEET; no detection meter                                                                            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00715_582f2592adb4","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Sparrow             | Teacher       | Day Call                          | Learned through Teaching Practice and expressed through Gathering Place; no call-learning subsystem                                                      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00716_564edd151384","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Toad                | Caretaker     | Cool Keeping / Wet-Ground Keeping | While present and available, applies the reduced global Perishable decay rate; does not stack with advanced Caretaking                                   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00717_1b9311e7960a","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Firefly Family      | Leader        | Lantern Procession                | Illuminates one bounded route or Place during an eligible night Home MEET; does not extend the workday                                                   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00718_057b3e8ae751","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Groundhog           | Gardener      | Seasonal Telegraph                | Reads an existing authored or scheduled seasonal pressure; no weather simulation                                                                         |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00719_5a9a1e833d26","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Turtle              | Caretaker     | Protected Receiving               | During an eligible crisis or Homecoming, protects one chosen bounded stake from an immediate consequence; event-specific, not storage                    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00720_ed07b71f9653","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Bumblebee Household | Gardener      | Carry the Bloom                   | An exceptional flowering plant recovered Away may persist through a Garden Project; no baseline Harvest bonus or pollination simulation                  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00721_a972a22d357e","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Mole                | Builder       | Subsurface Diagnosis              | An event- or Telegraph-based diagnosis opens a better Builder response or Project; no soil simulation                                                    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00722_dbd67431449b","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Bat                 | Builder       | Dry-Dark Inspection               | In an eligible Home MEET involving an enclosed or inaccessible structure, reveals source or extent and opens a response; no structure-decay layer        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00723_3556c8e8cddc","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Pigeon              | Leader        | Correspondence                    | Send Word, Ask the Flock, delayed answers, Promises, MEETs, and destinations; not automatically a Project                                                |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00724_16cb05c2b6cc","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Skunk               | Watchkeeper   | Boundary Deterrence               | Nonlethal local response with descriptive aftermath; no universal Scent Condition                                                                        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00725_a45fe2c40032","block_type":"table_row","section":"5.3 Resident Guest alignment","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"| Opossum             | Healer        | Aftermath Receiving               | At Homecoming or Home MEET, isolates one questionable Cargo quantity, returning Item, carcass, or affected Citizen; no contamination or quarantine meter |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00745_13af75479739","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Raccoon - HANDLE - Latchwork","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.1¶1-->
Opens a suitable sealed or latched human container or simple mechanism. The result may be Resources, an Item, a MEET, danger, contamination, nothing useful, or a later RENDER opportunity. Opening does not process contents, identify hazards, increase Cargo, bypass unrelated Tools, or auto-convert the object into Scrap.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00750_26301b937b66","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Crow - READ - Long View","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.2¶1-->
Reveals bounded distant context: Reach character, movement, route change, Crossing pressure, Outpost activity, approaching party or predator, or a likely Node function. It does not clear whole-Reach Fog, replace exploration, provide exact quantities, or grant aerial fast travel.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00755_2be0d1d80a07","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Fox - HANDLE - Carcass Claim; embodied RENDER access","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.3¶1-->
Approaches and secures a suitable carcass opportunity and recovers its authored Sustenance yield. At a suitable carcass Node, Fox may perform the available Node-authored RENDER without carrying a conventional Render Tool. RENDER consumes the specified material and makes the named Supply. Fox does not preserve Sustenance, ignore Cargo, neutralize contamination, prevent rivals, or create a separate carcass-crafting system.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00760_7ca7e6819d37","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Weasel - INTERCEDE - Drive Off","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.4¶1-->
Redirects or pursues a suitable threat, creates an escape interval, protects a vulnerable subject, or opens WITHDRAW. It uses ordinary RISK, MEET, injury, and separation. It creates no combat subsystem, chase minigame, or universal size table.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00765_ef8c6f68bbfa","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Hedgehog - INTERCEDE - Living Cover","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.5¶1-->
Protects or escorts one vulnerable Citizen or one discrete Item during exposed movement or withdrawal. It does not protect the entire party, anonymous Cargo quantities, or negate traffic and danger.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00770_1189e27a321b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Snake - SPEAK - Display","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.6¶1-->
Opens intimidation, recognition, nonverbal communication, PARLEY, YIELD, or controlled withdrawal in narrowly authored contexts. It is not a translator, attack, forced surrender, or general social bonus.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00775_77baa225f267","block_type":"paragraph","section":"Mink - REACH - Water Reach","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"<!--@5.5.7¶1-->
Enters water, flooded culverts, drainage channels, submerged passages, and other authored water domains to inspect, retrieve, rescue, or access a Node. It does not ferry the party, create fast travel, remove Exposure, guarantee recovery, or automatically RENDER recovered matter.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00787_22a61bef08fe","block_type":"list_item","section":"5.6 Guest relationship to Tool grammar","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"  - Raccoon may expose a later RENDER opportunity; Crow may reveal one; Weasel may create time or space for another Citizen to act; Hedgehog may protect a Citizen or discrete Item; Snake may preserve social access; Mink may reach the Node.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001__B00790_f4d159939846","block_type":"list_item","section":"5.6 Guest relationship to Tool grammar","source_id":"M050-SRC-GDD-COVERAGE-GAP-001","source_text":"  - Fox is the only current Expedition Guest with standing embodied access to Node-authored RENDER.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00547_19187decf2b4","block_type":"paragraph","section":"13.2 Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@13.2¶1-->
A Firefly Family is animated as a loose, recognizable cloud of approximately five or six lights. The family is known by formation, pulse, and route. Its civic action is shared illumination.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00552_44bc4a72e28e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"13.3 Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@13.3¶1-->
A Bumblebee Household is represented by several prominently animated bees and known by circulation, hum, and repeated return to one House. Its one Gardener Capacity is global across constructed Gardens. The game does not simulate individual pollination routes or diagnose each Garden separately.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00676_d24eef5737b3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18. Detailed Expedition Guest Roster","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19¶1-->
The seven Expedition species cover the shared Permission families without requiring an eighth species merely for symmetry. Two INTERCEDE entries are retained because their verbs are materially different: Weasel acts against the threat; Hedgehog acts around the vulnerable party. Each entry includes an illustrative named Citizen and Home Role, but Expedition Home Roles remain individual-authored rather than universal species locks.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00681_6343db1a7deb","block_type":"table_row","section":"18. Detailed Expedition Guest Roster","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| Raccoon             | HANDLE - Latchwork       | Latch               | Crafter               | Raised Box / Salvage Loft             |

Detailed Expedition Guest Roster","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| American Mink       | REACH - Water Reach      | Reed                | Builder               | Waterline Lodge / High-Water Refuge   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00696_5a624618eaf6","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Crafter       |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00697_a57ddd223ec8","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | HANDLE - Latchwork             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00698_e971f6d5a686","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Raised Box / Salvage Loft      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00699_fb3f24c33e45","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Dexterous handling and sorting |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00701_cee542a9059a","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.1¶2-->
**Species identity.** Dexterous forepaws, comfort with human refuse, curiosity, material intelligence, and a socially canny relationship to possession make the Raccoon the roster's clearest human-object specialist.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00703_1e8d2695cba7","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.1¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Latchwork opens sealed or latched human containers and mechanisms at a Node: coolers, capped vessels, tied bags, bin lids, simple catches, and similar objects. The Raccoon makes handling possible; the party still decides whether the object is worth opening and bears whatever the contents attract or release.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00705_bb6154473d65","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.1¶4-->
**Limits.** Latchwork does not identify contamination, guarantee useful contents, remove carrying cost, or turn every human mechanism into a solvable puzzle. The Independent Impulse is first inspection: in authored moments the Raccoon may be drawn to test the shut thing before the party has fully settled the surrounding risk.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00707_22f22e3439ca","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.1¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A dry raised box, reclaimed human container, or trunk-mounted loft includes a sorting shelf and direct exterior access. Mouse JOIN makes it a receiving loft attached to the Manor; Rabbit GATHER faces it toward the outer court; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a stable box-node. Clicks, lids, sorted objects, and a visible personal collection alter Home.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00709_ab9ff16c52f1","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.1¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Test a latch with forepaws, rotate an unfamiliar object, sort a collection by touch, or rest inside the raised box while traffic light passes across the opening.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00711_88178d99cd5e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.1. Raccoon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.1¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - LATCH<br />
</strong>Latch is first met inside a service-area waste bin, trapped after opening a lid that will not release from within. The Terms require a dry raised box and one shelf that no Council inventory may claim. Quick-handed and suspicious of waste, Latch contributes as a Crafter at Home. A Core Crafter admires the object fluency; the Leader resents Latch's habit of opening before asking. The remembered image is a row of carefully cleaned useless keys above the House entrance.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00720_7c4240440043","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Teacher     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00721_2a5d22398ad7","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | READ - Long View             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00722_2bbeb53dbb39","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | High Perch / Open Nest       |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00723_a4185ebc1f14","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Distant observation and call |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00725_67959e7b33f3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.2¶2-->
**Species identity.** Aerial perspective, location memory, call-based communication, curiosity, and the ability to connect distant signs give the Crow a view of the corridor that no ground-bound Citizen possesses.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00727_5cf61dbec9b3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.2¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Long View reveals context before commitment: movement beyond cover, the rough shape of a Node, a changed route, an approaching party, or the fact that an apparent opening ends in danger. The Permission gives the expedition a better question to answer rather than the answer itself.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00729_f40c9d2a9119","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.2¶4-->
**Limits.** The Crow does not provide omniscience, exact future prediction, aerial fast travel, or a safe Crossing bypass. The Independent Impulse is widening the look: an unusual glint, call, or movement may draw the Crow beyond the strict briefing and create a new piece of context with its own cost.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00731_db14b7202683","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.2¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A high open perch or nest needs broad sightlines, safe landing, and no enclosing roof. Mouse JOIN reaches it through a protected wall loft; Rabbit GATHER lets it overlook the common court; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a high node with redundant approaches. Calls become part of the Colony clock.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00733_282c31e85f72","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.2¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Turn among distant sounds, watch traffic patterns from above, make a short safe circuit between perches, preen, or sit through a weather change while Home moves below.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00735_5f855f4e553d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.2. Crow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.2¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - SLATE<br />
</strong>Slate is first met on a sound-wall cap, watching truck rhythm to recover a dropped bright ring. The Terms require a west-facing perch with an unobstructed launch and permission to be absent for solitary day flights. Slate contributes as a Teacher, turning route memory into lessons rather than serving as a permanent alarm. A young Citizen becomes an eager student; an established Watchkeeper dislikes Slate's unscheduled departures. The House is known as Slate's High Room.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00744_c9a62a713a8b","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Caretaker            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00745_68087c9b1d31","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | HANDLE - Carcass Claim                |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00746_0edd4a58135d","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Perimeter Earth / Meat-Handling Apron |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00747_95a92ae19da3","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Scent, digging, and boundary rest     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00749_58f024ed9c5b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.3¶2-->
**Species identity.** Large body, scent-led perception, predator silhouette, and competence around carcasses make the Fox both materially valuable and socially difficult. The Colony must welcome the individual without pretending inherited prey fear has vanished.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00751_11f8e9db4efb","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.3¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Carcass Claim allows the expedition to approach, portion, and make use of a major roadkill or carcass windfall that smaller animals cannot safely handle. It opens decisions about what to take, what to leave, how long to remain, and what attention the work may draw.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00753_fae4f9b1f4ba","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.3¶4-->
**Limits.** The Fox does not automatically carry the windfall, make it safe to eat, prevent rival scavengers, or remove the moral and social consequences of the scene. The Independent Impulse is claim: the Fox expects a fair share and resists abandoning usable food without reason.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00755_80e1f948b88c","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.3¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A substantial earth at the Colony boundary requires direct outer access, drainage, and a handling surface away from Nursery and clean stores. Mouse JOIN uses a defended outer passage; Rabbit GATHER includes the entrance in social frontage without centering it; Squirrel CONNECT links a low earth node to upper refuge routes.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00757_93bcc08759ee","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.3¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Read the outer edge by scent, dig and arrange bedding, carry food to the apron, curl into the earth, or learn which Colony smells now mean safety.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00759_52b17ebaeee2","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.3. Red Fox","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.3¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - BRACKEN<br />
</strong>Bracken is first met at a deer carcass during a lean autumn, initially refusing the expedition any share. A successful PARLEY creates a recurring division of the windfall and eventually an invitation. The Terms require a perimeter earth, a clean handling apron, and a rule against surprise entry through the young Citizens' path. Bracken contributes as a Caretaker. One household trusts the careful food work; another still freezes when the Fox crosses the court. That unresolved bodily truth is part of the relationship.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00768_e0f5d12b7938","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Watchkeeper   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00769_11ded846ae67","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | INTERCEDE - Drive Off          |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00770_c9d9352e2201","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Bank Den / Narrow Patrol Run   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00771_8b4bf7c5e74b","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Fast bank movement and pursuit |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00773_5189d9519802","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.4¶2-->
**Species identity.** Narrow body, explosive speed, intense attention, and willingness to press a smaller predator outward define the Weasel as an active intercessor rather than a general combat unit.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00775_73547de530fa","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.4¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Drive Off opens a response against a small predator or aggressive animal: pursue, force away from the vulnerable party, pin attention elsewhere, or create an interval for escape. The action changes the geometry of danger; it does not erase it.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00777_ba715b233794","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.4¶4-->
**Limits.** The Permission does not guarantee victory and exposes the Weasel to injury or separation. The Independent Impulse is pursuit: once committed, the Weasel may carry the chase farther than the party prefers, creating a real WITHDRAW or recovery decision.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00779_b30d64f1157e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.4¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A narrow bank den needs compact tunnels, several exits, and a readable shared threshold. Mouse JOIN attaches it to an exterior run; Rabbit GATHER places the entrance at a court edge; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a low patrol node linked to escape routes. Sudden movement becomes part of Home life.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00781_cca2b922c55d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.4¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Move through a bank run, inspect small openings, burst across a short patrol route, play within a safe corridor, or groom after returning to the den.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00783_50ff5089b9fc","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.4. Weasel","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.4¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - RILL<br />
</strong>Rill is first met driving rats from a drainage seam that the expedition needs to cross. The Terms require a bank den with freedom to patrol beyond the immediate boundary and no promise to ignore every rival scent. Rill contributes as a Watchkeeper at Home. The senior Watchkeeper values the patrol instincts; the Healer is exhausted by preventable cuts. The den is called the Quick Bank.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00792_69ce2283b54f","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Healer      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00793_44996d8fae24","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | INTERCEDE - Living Cover     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00794_06a40f1626dd","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Hedge Hollow / Leaf Run      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00795_f56ac8e7ff4b","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Protected movement and trust |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00797_5d17d170074e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.5¶2-->
**Species identity.** Spines, deliberate pace, low protected body, and a vulnerable face and underside create a form of defense based on sheltering and escort rather than aggression.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00799_ce6a35db3053","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.5¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Living Cover allows the Hedgehog to escort an injured or very small Citizen, shield fragile cargo, or create cover during a withdrawal across exposed ground. The Permission keeps vulnerability moving when ordinary retreat would leave it behind.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00801_5ebca2126e41","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.5¶4-->
**Limits.** The Hedgehog cannot ignore traffic, protect an entire party, or attack every threat. The Independent Impulse is refusal to abandon: once committed to a vulnerable companion, the Hedgehog may accept delay rather than leave them.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00803_3bd706bbc893","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.5¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A dense hedge hollow needs leaf litter, concealment, a quiet run, and enough shared access for care. Mouse JOIN makes it an exterior hedge room; Rabbit GATHER uses it as protective court fringe; Squirrel CONNECT links the low refuge to several routes upward.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00805_132d0227b47b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.5¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Forage beneath leaves, test a hedge passage, curl and slowly relax, or walk beside a smaller friend through protected ground.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00807_102a9d052b2b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.5. Hedgehog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.5¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - BURDOCK<br />
</strong>Burdock is first met sheltering an injured Mouse beneath a roadside hedge after a failed Crossing. The Terms require a dense leaf hollow and a path wide enough for another Citizen to walk beside it. Burdock contributes as a Healer, especially in recovery companionship. A timid young Rabbit becomes inseparable; a hurried expedition veteran struggles with Burdock's refusal to leave anyone behind. The House is simply Burdock Hedge.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00816_162d4cfdcb88","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Teacher             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00817_a05ffafe169a","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | SPEAK - Display                      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00818_eff26d1997c1","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Warm-Stone Shelter / Scent Threshold |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00819_37c226770f10","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Basking and scent-reading            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00821_be27ee777684","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.6¶2-->
**Species identity.** Limbless movement, scent-led perception, warmth dependence, silent display, and inherited prey fear make the Garter Snake a powerful test of whether equal citizenship can preserve bodily difference.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00823_79d98baf8473","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.6¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Display opens intimidation, recognition, or nonverbal communication with animals that understand snake posture and threat. It may create a PARLEY, YIELD, or withdrawal option where ordinary speech has no force.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00825_4376de3d2e29","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.6¶4-->
**Limits.** Display is not a venom attack, universal translator, or guaranteed surrender. The Independent Impulse is stillness and presentation: when pressed, the Snake may choose to hold ground and become unmistakable rather than flee.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00827_01a0cf809548","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.6¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A south-facing warm-stone shelter needs protected cracks, basking surface, and a visible approach that prevents surprise encounters. Mouse JOIN attaches a heated wall chamber; Rabbit GATHER places a sunny shelf at the court edge; Squirrel CONNECT links the low warm node into safe routes.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00829_f65108b0f620","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.6¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Follow a sun patch, move through warm grass, test scent, coil inside a sheltered crack, or rest beside a trusted Citizen who has learned not to startle.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00831_64d6463829a7","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.6. Common Garter Snake","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.6¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - SEDGE<br />
</strong>Sedge is first met basking across the expedition's only safe concrete seam and refuses to move until the party acknowledges the territory. The Terms require a warm stone House and a Colony custom of announcing movement near its entrance. Sedge contributes as a Teacher, sharing scent and ground knowledge rather than becoming a Watchkeeper. One young Citizen is fascinated; several Rabbits remain visibly uneasy. The custom of calling "warm side" before passing becomes part of Home etiquette.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00840_56342ec823c5","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Example Citizen: Builder             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00841_0a9b737261d7","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | REACH - Water Reach                  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00842_642dab9c00e8","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Waterline Lodge / High-Water Refuge  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00843_fc20dccd40c2","block_type":"table_row","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Swimming, diving, and waterline rest |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00845_43c7e589ba1f","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.7¶2-->
**Species identity.** Water competence, sleek speed, culvert familiarity, and a powerful rescue impulse make the Mink the expedition's access to water as a lived domain rather than a generic terrain modifier.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00847_bfd1667c038b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.7¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Water Reach allows the Mink to enter water, flooded culverts, drainage channels, or waterlogged spaces to retrieve, inspect, or rescue where the ordinary party cannot safely go.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00849_0be6b5db9dfb","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.7¶4-->
**Limits.** The Mink does not ferry the party, eliminate cold or current, make floodwater clean, or guarantee recovery. The Independent Impulse is immediate rescue: when a life is visibly in danger, the Mink may enter before the Council has finished deciding.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00851_c0125be1bd7e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.7¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A waterline lodge needs direct water entry, a dry interior, and refuge above ordinary flood rise. Mouse JOIN attaches it to a culvert annex; Rabbit GATHER places it beside a protected pool; Squirrel CONNECT treats it as a low water node with several routes upward.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00853_9ca28a46a6fb","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.7¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Swim a protected channel, dive beneath roots, groom at the lodge entrance, or float quietly while watching Home from water level.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00855_89f612966ea3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"18.7. American Mink","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@18.7¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - REED<br />
</strong>Reed is first met pulling a stranded Squirrel from runoff before either Colony or expedition has chosen sides. The Terms require a lodge with direct water access and a high-water chamber that remains connected to Home. Reed contributes as a Builder, taking responsibility for waterline structures. The Builder trusts Reed's reading of current; the Leader fears the rescue impulse will someday outrun the party. Wet tracks between the lodge and Council become an ordinary part of dawn.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00874_a6d08c9583f1","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.
