"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00875_3a9982394ddc","block_type":"table_row","section":"19. Detailed Resident Guest Roster","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| Striped Skunk       | Watchkeeper    | Boundary Deterrence             | Sable               | Individual Citizen        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00876_478625d50a8f","block_type":"table_row","section":"19. Detailed Resident Guest Roster","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| Virginia Opossum    | Healer         | Aftermath Receiving             | Morrow              | Individual Citizen        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00885_c58a9dbbc82d","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Watchkeeper - fixed Guest Practice    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00886_5887d16a48a2","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Night Sky-watch                       |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00887_0ec5126b53fb","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | High Hollow / Accessible Roost        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00888_a54094088f27","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Nocturnal listening and high presence |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00890_c43377b368db","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.1¶2-->
**Species identity.** Nocturnal hearing, high perspective, quiet patience, and a body built for night establish the Owl as a resident whose warning is sensory rather than numerical.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00892_f99e1f7da5c3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.1¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Night Sky-watch gives a nocturnal predator or unusual night movement earlier or clearer Telegraph when the Owl is present and the High Hollow is usable. The Affordance may identify direction, behavior, or the fact that the movement is not ordinary weather.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00894_e0255c9e06c5","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.1¶4-->
**Limits.** The Owl does not provide universal detection, daytime coverage, exact distance, or automatic defense. If injury, weather, disturbance, or House damage prevents listening, the Affordance is unavailable.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00896_160436f105c8","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.1¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A dry dark high hollow needs a broad listening opening and species-appropriate access. Mouse JOIN reaches it through a protected loft or ramp; Rabbit GATHER lets it overlook the common ground without dominating it; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a high stable node. The Colony's night soundscape changes around the resident calls.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00898_acf3cd84f214","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.1¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Listen while the Colony settles, turn toward sounds other Citizens cannot hear, groom within the hollow, or watch moonlit traffic from a safe opening.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00900_1cf71f42631f","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.1. Barred Owl","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.1¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - WHOOT<br />
</strong>WHOOT is a barred owl with a permanently weak wing, first met grounded after a storm and surviving by listening from a broken sign cavity. The Terms require an accessible high hollow that can be reached without full flight. WHOOT contributes one Watchkeeper Capacity and provides Night Sky-watch. A young Citizen learns the night calls; an older Watchkeeper initially resents advice from someone who cannot patrol. The first winter in which WHOOT hears a fox before anyone else becomes a defining Tale.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00909_93850d6f34b8","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Teacher - fixed Guest Practice                |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00910_414038ef2eb7","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Day Call                                      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00911_b048ffa2896a","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Circle Nest / Court-Side Shrub                |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00912_68d10d62339e","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Song, call recognition, and seasonal presence |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00914_77124a74fae5","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.2¶2-->
**Species identity.** Learned calls, seasonal song, repeated perches, and the gradual ability of other Citizens to understand one named bird make the Songbird a cultural resident rather than another generic alarm.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00916_b6c819da9f3e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.2¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Day Call opens an alarm or rally response during aerial danger or sudden daylight disruption. Scattered Citizens recognize that the same situation is occurring and may gather, shelter, or follow a coordinated instruction before confusion separates them.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00918_6ab5f8cae5d1","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.2¶4-->
**Limits.** Day Call does not detect every threat, prevent panic automatically, or create a colony-wide morale modifier. It depends on the Songbird being present and the Colony having learned the calls through ordinary life.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00920_58c138e3675d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.2¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A small nest needs concealment, a clear singing perch, and social proximity. Mouse JOIN uses a planted wall room or exterior niche; Rabbit GATHER places the nest above the Story Circle; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a modest branch node near a shared junction. Seasonal songs enter the memory of Home.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00922_1bf98134dc58","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.2¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Sing from familiar points, bathe in shallow water, gather nesting material, or sit with the Colony as individual calls acquire shared meaning.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00924_30e03b90def3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.2. Song Sparrow","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.2¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - LILT<br />
</strong>Lilt returns to the same thorn shrub for three springs before a storm destroys the old nesting ground. The Terms require a concealed nest overlooking the Story Circle and a quiet interval at dawn. Lilt contributes as Teacher. Young Citizens learn the difference between food call, alarm, and ordinary song; an Elder remembers the first season by which melody was heard. If the nest later falls silent, the whole court feels the absence before the roster is opened.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00932_be82670fa5c0","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Citizen form**      | Individual Citizen                            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00933_493da46a9df1","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Caretaker - fixed Guest Practice              |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00934_4b6a720dd0a6","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Wet-Ground and Store Protection               |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00935_990b1b48b944","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Rain Niche / Culvert House with Dry Refuge    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00936_11ff1f62ad56","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Warm rain, stillness, and wet-ground movement |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00938_83f7c616fbd1","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.3¶2-->
**Species identity.** Dampness, stillness, runoff familiarity, and a body that moves between wet ground and dry refuge make the Toad a domestic interpreter of water where it meets stores and inhabited space.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00940_25e27a7a203c","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.3¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** During runoff, damp-storage, culvert, or contamination situations, the Toad opens a response that separates threatened stores, redirects shallow water, identifies what remains safe, or protects one domestic stake from spreading wet damage.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00942_40d6408ec201","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.3¶4-->
**Limits.** The Affordance is not a permanent spoilage reduction, water purification aura, or flood immunity. It applies only where wetness and domestic consequence meaningfully meet.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00944_bc1d5ae83be9","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.3¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A damp niche needs leaf cover, a shallow wet approach, and an elevated dry refuge. Mouse JOIN builds it into a culvert-facing exterior room; Rabbit GATHER places it beside controlled wet ground at the court edge; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a low rain node with routes upward.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00946_fdd01273ce65","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.3¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Sit in warm rain, move through wet leaves, wait in stillness, or make a small feeding movement as dusk reaches the House.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00948_8d1a01f7bb36","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.3. American Toad","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.3¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - SUMP<br />
</strong>Sump is first met in a flooded drainage hollow, repeatedly returning to the same dry bottle-cap ledge as water rises. The Terms require a damp chamber and a dry shelf above the ordinary runoff line. Sump contributes as Caretaker and provides Wet-Ground and Store Protection. A household Cook trusts Sump's judgment about wet food; a Gardener finds the stillness unnerving. The Rain Niche becomes the Place where children first learn that water has several different sounds.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00956_e4d2ade4d604","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Citizen form**      | Collective-bodied Citizen - one named family, usually five or six visible lights |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00957_c82a7860d5b3","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Leader - fixed Guest Practice                                                    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00958_93dd5a71a0ab","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Lantern Procession                                                               |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00959_0572ad225caa","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Dusk Hollow / Lantern Garden                                                     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00960_5ade27cf0837","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Loose constellation and shared illumination                                      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00962_33c0ba1e7c07","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.4¶2-->
**Species identity.** The Firefly Family is known as one small luminous household whose formation, pulse, and route are more legible than any single tiny body. Their civic identity is coordinated light.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00964_8178ac718b38","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.4¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Lantern Procession illuminates one bounded route or small Place during a night Home MEET: an evacuation path, Healing Place, urgent Council, flood edge, or final dark approach for a returning party. The family allows scattered Citizens to act together in darkness.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00966_87bf89c6df8d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.4¶4-->
**Limits.** The Affordance does not extend the universal workday, light several Places at once, remove night pressure, or behave as permanent infrastructure. The lights gather and go somewhere; choosing one route means leaving another dark.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00968_2bb779dc4e6a","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.4¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A protected grass hollow needs damp leaf litter, darkness by day, an open evening flight space, and freedom from harsh artificial light. Mouse JOIN creates a planted dark court attached to the Manor; Rabbit GATHER places it at the common's quiet edge; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a ground-level glow node linked to higher routes.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00970_08a707d194b9","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.4¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Guide the family as a loose constellation, widen or narrow the formation, pause above one Place, accompany first emergence, or follow one lagging light until it rejoins the others.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00972_a63a4f92a2b0","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.4. Firefly Family","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.4¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - THE LANTERNS<br />
</strong>The Lanterns are six recurring lights first seen gathering around a lost young Citizen at the edge of the median, making the safe grass route visible. The Terms require a protected Dusk Hollow and a Colony rule against bright flame near it. They contribute as one Leader Capacity and provide Lantern Procession. Young Citizens learn each light's habitual place in the formation. After a hard storm, only five lights return; the missing space becomes visible Campaign Memory without creating a separate roster death.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00981_bff0e32235fe","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Gardener - fixed Guest Practice    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00982_453160d94def","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Seasonal Telegraph                 |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00983_cc850d281991","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Deep Perimeter Burrow / Lookout    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00984_7b7dbb788ba9","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Soil, lookout, and seasonal change |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00986_67c12f7e0808","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.5¶2-->
**Species identity.** Deep burrowing, upright weather-reading, seasonal rhythm, and attention to changing ground make the Groundhog a Gardener whose knowledge concerns the timing of green life rather than individual plots.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00988_acddd889a3e5","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.5¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Seasonal Telegraph identifies the family of an approaching pressure before the Council commits its posture: hard frost rather than an ordinary cold night, flood rather than ordinary rain, heat stress, disruptive human work, or another major seasonal turn.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00990_a5e0d93f5c18","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.5¶4-->
**Limits.** The Groundhog does not provide an exact forecast, countdown, guaranteed severity, or universal warning. The information remains qualitative and may still leave difficult choices.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00992_7e172b183b7c","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.5¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A deep perimeter burrow needs drainage, more than one safe entrance, an undisturbed ground volume, and a visible lookout. Mouse JOIN links it through a defended outer passage; Rabbit GATHER places the lookout toward the court; Squirrel CONNECT makes the burrow a low seasonal node tied to several routes.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00994_2111a9b0d4dd","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.5¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Stand upright to read weather, clear a burrow entrance, sun on the lookout, or accompany the first bodily response to seasonal change.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B00996_6752b7cf1e0c","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.5. Groundhog","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.5¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - ROOTWAKE<br />
</strong>Rootwake is first met repeatedly filling a shallow trench before a road crew arrives, behavior the expedition initially mistakes for territorial fussing. The Terms require a deep burrow, a lookout mound, and a promise that no later Project will build across the tunnels. Rootwake contributes as Gardener and provides Seasonal Telegraph. The Builder sometimes resents the protected ground; the Colony learns that Rootwake changes routine before the sky explains why.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01004_dfe0c4cd6851","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Citizen form**      | Individual Citizen                   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01005_97d0b1c20b87","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Caretaker - fixed Guest Practice     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01006_7d1f1e271bf9","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Protected Receiving                  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01007_a351047c3534","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Stonewater Chamber / Basking Shelf   |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01008_205a62693563","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Patience, basking, and shallow water |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01010_cfe5ddc93b3e","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.6¶2-->
**Species identity.** Shell, deliberate movement, water access, and temporal patience make the Turtle a resident of continuity and safe holding rather than speed or output.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01012_990ee50ff5a0","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.6¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Protected Receiving allows one explicitly chosen reserve, fragile Record, medicine stock, unusual returning object, or other bounded stake to be held safely during a relevant crisis. The selection is made before impact or as part of Telegraph and response.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01014_7080d28e58fb","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.6¶4-->
**Limits.** The chamber is not automatic insurance for all stores, a generic armor bonus, or unlimited secure inventory. Protecting one stake may mean leaving another exposed.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01016_74d0fcbe27a2","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.6¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A sunk stone chamber needs shallow water access, a basking shelf, and a protected dry interior. Mouse JOIN attaches a pool chamber to the Manor edge; Rabbit GATHER makes it part of a quiet communal water garden; Squirrel CONNECT treats it as a stable low node with routes to higher refuge.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01018_97d974de496d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.6¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Bask, enter shallow water, move slowly through a garden path, or watch highway light travel across the surface.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01020_bce92bf37219","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.6. Painted Turtle","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.6¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - STILLWATER<br />
</strong>Stillwater is first met stranded in a drainage pool that is drying faster than the Turtle can leave it. The Terms require a shallow permanent pool, warm stone, and a chamber that remains dry through ordinary rain. Stillwater contributes as Caretaker and provides Protected Receiving. A Teacher values the unhurried presence; impatient Citizens learn that some decisions can be held without being forgotten. The Stonewater Chamber later protects the first written Colony Record during a flood.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01028_7429a1894b41","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Citizen form**      | Collective-bodied Citizen - one named household represented by several visible bees |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01029_30cf2e0800af","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Gardener - fixed Guest Practice                                                     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01030_564b2ccd0c66","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Carry the Bloom                                                                     |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01031_7f47d461030c","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Moss House / Bee Garden                                                             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01032_63399c7af821","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Hum, warmth, and coordinated flower work                                            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01034_d11775b1852f","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.7¶2-->
**Species identity.** A Bumblebee Household is known through circulation, hum, repeated return, and collective work. Several visible bodies produce one legible civic subject without creating a hidden bee civilization or honey economy.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01036_bc387b221fcb","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.7¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** The household contributes one global Gardener Capacity across all constructed Gardens. Carry the Bloom allows an exceptional flowering plant recovered Away to become a persistent cultivated line through an ordinary Garden Project, or allows a threatened rare line to survive by sacrificing present yield and committing civic effort.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01038_54b06be0adf4","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.7¶4-->
**Limits.** The game does not assign bees to individual Gardens, simulate pollination routes, diagnose plot health, increase all yields, or make ordinary farming dependent on Guests. Carry the Bloom applies to exceptional continuity, not baseline agriculture.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01040_9b8099ac2b81","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.7¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A protected moss-lined cavity needs warmth, shelter from hard rain and flooding, a clear flight opening, and broad non-mechanical access to flowering space. Mouse JOIN places it in a planted exterior chamber; Rabbit GATHER uses a flower bank at the court edge; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a garden node linked through the Web.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01042_d06c5383641d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.7¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Accompany the household through an impressionistic sequence of Gardens, feel vibration and warmth at first emergence, shelter as wind rises, or return to the House through the familiar opening.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01044_bd6740650d76","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.7. Bumblebee Household","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.7¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - THE GOLDWINGS<br />
</strong>The Goldwings are first met working a rare roadside flower after mowing destroys their former nest. The Terms require a warm Moss House, protected flower access, and no smoke near the opening. They contribute one Gardener Capacity across all Gardens and provide Carry the Bloom. A Gardener later brings home the same roadside flower; with the Goldwings it becomes a lasting Colony planting. Years later the bloom beside the Nursery remembers both household and expedition.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01053_e4dd150a6888","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Builder - fixed Guest Practice             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01054_a3cc688a67dc","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Subsurface Diagnosis                       |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01055_08263cbf2778","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Visible Cutaway Tunnel House / Mound Court |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01056_265540fc8bfa","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Soil listening and bounded digging         |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01058_6d5466af995b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.8¶2-->
**Species identity.** Ground vibration, soil movement, hidden voids, and a body adapted to digging make the Mole a Builder who reveals what the Colony cannot see beneath its Places.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01060_50ff42e118d3","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.8¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Subsurface Diagnosis may reveal saturated soil, hidden void, undercutting water, severed root structure, frost-heaved ground, or buried obstruction before visible collapse. The information can make a preventive Builder Project or different MEET response possible.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01062_0f572cbbb5c4","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.8¶4-->
**Limits.** The Mole does not create a hidden underground civilization, automatically excavate new rooms, reveal arbitrary treasure, or make structures immune to failure.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01064_0966ee2c9076","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.8¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** The House is a bounded, readable cutaway tunnel system with visible entrances and mounds. Mouse JOIN integrates it beside an exterior foundation; Rabbit GATHER lets mounds define a court edge; Squirrel CONNECT makes the low soil Place part of several surface routes. The no-underground doctrine remains intact because the resident stays visually legible.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01066_8eedb18c9a14","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.8¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Dig a short safe run, listen through soil, shape loose earth, or emerge through a familiar sheltered opening.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01068_b6c0bfa85227","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.8. Eastern Mole","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.8¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - MARL<br />
</strong>Marl is first met when a new tunnel breaks into an undercut bank and the Mole repeatedly blocks the expedition from crossing it. The Terms require a defined ground volume and visible entrances that Colony construction will respect. Marl contributes as Builder and provides Subsurface Diagnosis. A Builder learns to trust the sudden appearance of fresh mounds; a Squirrel finds the unseen movement deeply uncomfortable. The House is called Marl Below, though it remains visible in cutaway.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01077_b30d4053f630","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Builder - fixed Guest Practice    |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01078_1e2872f8b5f3","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Dry-Dark Structure Care           |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01079_096d1e60e369","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | High Dry Roost / Flight Aperture  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01080_22cb4657f200","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Echo, hanging, and dusk departure |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01082_473e0218ef4c","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.9¶2-->
**Species identity.** Echolocation, sensitivity to enclosed air, roosting in dry darkness, and local flight make the Bat a structural resident of spaces other Citizens rarely inspect.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01084_b6fff63ac2aa","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.9¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Dry-Dark Structure Care reveals damp, rot, insect pressure, obstructed airflow, or another change inside high enclosed structure before the resulting damage becomes obvious. It may open inspection, ventilation, or localized repair responses.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01086_469b9f6f64fd","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.9¶4-->
**Limits.** The Bat does not eliminate structural decay, monitor the entire Colony at once, replace Builder Capacity, or become a night Watchkeeper merely because flight occurs after dusk.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01088_b19aba0f1837","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.9¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A high dry dark roost needs hanging space, stable temperature, a clear flight aperture, and freedom from smoke. Mouse JOIN makes it an upper wall chamber; Rabbit GATHER places it above the court with flight kept clear of busy ground; Squirrel CONNECT integrates it as a sheltered high node.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01090_2bde7adf6516","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.9¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Hang and groom, turn toward returning echoes, make a short dusk circuit, or experience Home through sound and changing air.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01092_496b617d9ae4","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.9. Little Brown Bat","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.9¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - VELVET<br />
</strong>Velvet is first met roosting inside a cracked highway reflector box after human work seals the former cavity. The Terms require a smoke-free high roost and an unobstructed evening aperture. Velvet contributes as Builder and provides Dry-Dark Structure Care. A Crafter is fascinated by echolocation; a young Citizen fears the silent returns until a repeated dusk routine becomes familiar. Velvet is the first to hear water moving inside a wall after winter thaw.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01101_e6bd24336690","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Leader - fixed Guest Practice              |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01102_95f7bf8f9ffc","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Correspondence                             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01103_31bab9e22433","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Ledge Loft / Open Flight Shelf             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01104_9555468145fb","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Built-environment flight and social signal |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01106_ad50114ae1bf","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.10¶2-->
**Species identity.** Landmark memory, social signaling, comfort with human structures, and movement among distant flock sites give the Pigeon a civic relationship to outside communities rather than a combat or scouting package.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01108_ad502af98037","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.10¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Correspondence opens a Send Word, Ask the Flock, or identify-the-origin response in situations involving Wanderers, known settlements, the Metropolis, or unusual built-environment activity. The result may create a delayed answer, Promise, or short civic Project.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01110_595abc4b42e1","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.10¶4-->
**Limits.** Correspondence is not instant communication, guaranteed delivery, a permanent world map, or a substitute for expedition travel. The Pigeon may know routes and social traces without knowing every message's meaning.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01112_6169220c3895","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.10¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A dry ledge loft needs stable landing, open flight, and visibility to distant structures. Mouse JOIN attaches it to a wall or sign loft; Rabbit GATHER places it above communal frontage; Squirrel CONNECT makes it a broad stable node. Cooing, circling, and occasional visitors enlarge the Colony's social horizon.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01114_3df48bc2aa2d","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.10¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Warm on a ledge, dust-bathe, head-bob through a shared Place, or make a short circle above Home and return to the same landmark.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01116_baa5e95edc72","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.10. Rock Pigeon","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.10¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - GABLE<br />
</strong>Gable is first met at an overpass carrying colored thread tied by another settlement, though the message is not immediately understood. The Terms require a dry ledge loft and a clear western flight lane. Gable contributes as Leader and provides Correspondence. The Council depends on the social reach; an expedition veteran distrusts answers that arrive through flock rumor. The first successful Send Word prevents a Wanderer family from reaching a closed route.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01125_f2b6933450cb","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Watchkeeper - fixed Guest Practice        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01126_eae9e9c399fd","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Boundary Deterrence                       |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01127_c02b34040aef","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Downwind Den / Perimeter Lane             |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01128_6dce457af3b7","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Deliberate dusk patrol and scent boundary |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01130_8c11f1ab6e95","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.11¶2-->
**Species identity.** Deliberate nocturnal movement, unmistakable warning, nonlethal deterrence, and a body that forces the Colony to negotiate proximity and airflow make the Skunk a Watchkeeper by boundary presence rather than surveillance.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01132_de4b5a166b80","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.11¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Boundary Deterrence opens a nonlethal drive-off response during predator or aggressive-scavenger Home MEET. The response can prevent direct Contest but usually creates a localized Scented Home aftermath affecting one Place, approach, or social situation.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01134_a9aff59ac217","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.11¶4-->
**Limits.** The Affordance is not automatic perfect defense, cannot be used without consequence in crowded interior space, and may be unavailable when wind, injury, or placement makes the response unsafe for the Colony.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01136_eac993561195","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.11¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A well-drained den needs a downwind perimeter position, clear approach, and separation from Nursery, food stores, and the Story Circle. Mouse JOIN uses a defended outer bank; Rabbit GATHER keeps the entrance visible from communal ground at respectful distance; Squirrel CONNECT links it as a low boundary node.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01138_3b8eb74d366b","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.11¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Walk a dusk boundary, root through leaves, test wind, mark a safe edge, or groom outside the den while Home keeps a respectful lane open.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01140_0f71bf06a5bb","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.11. Striped Skunk","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.11¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - SABLE<br />
</strong>Sable is first met standing between a young Rabbit and a coyote, holding the threat long enough for escape without fighting. The Terms require a downwind den and a clear perimeter lane no household will block. Sable contributes as Watchkeeper and provides Boundary Deterrence. The Watchkeepers respect the calm; Caretakers complain whenever the wind shifts after a response. The Colony eventually treats "Sable weather" as a practical civic phrase rather than a joke.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01149_d74446156492","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Role contribution** | Healer - fixed Guest Practice                  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01150_56ad1a3adfc5","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**         | Aftermath Receiving                            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01151_66ab29efab65","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**       | Dry Receiving Cavity / Dirty Edge              |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01152_0f7bb72c432f","block_type":"table_row","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY focus**      | Nocturnal cleanup, balance, and deep stillness |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01154_ce228775b47f","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.12¶2-->
**Species identity.** Nocturnal scavenging, careful handling of unpleasant remains, climbing, and the ability to become deeply still under danger make the Opossum a Healer of boundaries between injury, contamination, and ordinary Home.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01156_7af47fec0720","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.12¶3-->
**Mechanical expression.** Aftermath Receiving opens an isolation-and-cleanup response when Homecoming or Home MEET brings contaminated salvage, spoiled stores, a carcass, an unknown substance, or a potentially infectious patient. Broad contamination becomes a contained Cleanup, treatment, or temporary Place problem.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01158_d017208bfeac","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.12¶4-->
**Limits.** The Affordance does not erase illness, make contaminated material safe, grant biological immunity, or remove Caretaking and Healing Load. It changes the shape and spread of consequence.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01160_b999775922aa","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.12¶5-->
**Housing and colony flavor.** A dry cavity or reclaimed box needs a climbing route, ventilation, and placement near the receiving or refuse edge but apart from clean stores. Mouse JOIN makes it a controlled exterior receiving room; Rabbit GATHER places it at the court's service edge; Squirrel CONNECT links it to both receiving ground and upper retreat.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01162_ff85f9ffa7dd","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.12¶6-->
**EMBODY.** Move along a nocturnal receiving route, balance with the tail, arrange a sleeping cavity, inspect debris, or wake slowly while the Colony remains quiet.
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01164_e9511893d27a","block_type":"paragraph","section":"19.12. Virginia Opossum","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"<!--@19.12¶7-->
<table>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>EXAMPLE CITIZEN - MORROW<br />
</strong>Morrow is first met after a storm, calmly separating edible remains from contaminated debris while other scavengers avoid the site. The Terms require a dry box near the receiving edge and a firm separation from clean stores. Morrow contributes as Healer and provides Aftermath Receiving. The Healer values the calm during ugly work; a Crafter repeatedly brings questionable salvage too close. Morrow becomes the Citizen who meets returning parties before celebration begins.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01235_aa8327e38fe1","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Identity**             | Given or household name, species, silhouette, communication register, and character thesis.            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01236_bc2cfc379540","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Type**                 | Expedition or Resident, selected for play-experience reasons rather than social worth.                 |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01237_8d54cec0e5ac","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Citizen form**         | Individual or one of the two authorized collective-bodied households.                                  |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01238_3272e38fe7c5","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **First MEET**           | A circumstance in which the animal exists for its own reasons before recruitment is discussed.         |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01239_54c987778e6d","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Terms of Hospitality** | Concrete visible residence condition tied to body, place, safety, habit, or relationship.              |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01240_14258f3caf16","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Guest House**          | Mouse, Rabbit, and Squirrel translations; placement needs; folk naming direction.                      |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01241_976ffb7c5800","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Home life**            | Role Practice, routine, House use, absence consequence, relationships, and Home MEET hooks.            |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01242_2b803640b8a7","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Signature**            | Permission or Affordance with attribution, situation, limit, and suspension conditions.                |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01243_a9a39313b3fd","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Away package**         | For Expedition Guests: Permission family, Affinity, Independent Impulse, and shared-system exceptions. |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01244_fcfee08bbc47","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **EMBODY**               | At least one meaningful Presence concept and Practice / Flow where appropriate.                        |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001__B01245_cc79538fb37f","block_type":"table_row","section":"22.1 Required content fields for every Guest","source_id":"M050-SRC-GUEST-001","source_text":"| **Memory**               | Arrival, relationship, injury, departure, House history, loss, and Chronicle language.                 |
"},{"block_key":"M050-SRC-HUMAN-RULINGS-001__LOCATION__L00399-L00407","block_type":"legacy_record","section":"L00399-L00407","source_id":"M050-SRC-HUMAN-RULINGS-001","source_text":"Ecological Influences is active within a narrow translation scope: qualitative bodily priors, perceptions of safety and movement, ecology-versus-civilization boundaries, and privileged-camera doctrine.
